name: kinetics
label: Kinetics
description: Rate constants, half-lives and activation energies the paper reports for its experiments (runs when the paper mentions them).
system_prompt: Extract reaction kinetics. Report only what the paper states.
intro: This paper reports reaction kinetics. For each experiment set (and sample) in the structure plan below, extract the kinetic quantities the paper states for it: rate constants, half-lives, activation energies, and what they describe.
open_ended_hint: Further rate constants of a model with several reactions (k1, k2, ... or a1, b1, ...): one entry each, named by the constant and what it describes as the paper writes it (e.g. 'k1 Gly -> GlyGly', 'a2 (GG -> DKP)'), value with its unit as printed, category kinetics. Not concentrations or yields (another step records them), not the experimental conditions.

parameters.description: the observed (pseudo-)first-order rate constant of the row's main reaction (k, k_obs), in its printed unit (s-1, min-1, h-1).
a second-order rate constant of the row's main reaction (M-1 s-1, L mol-1 s-1).
the half-life of the reactant or product the paper names (say which in n).
activation energy (Ea, from an Arrhenius plot), kJ/mol or kcal/mol as printed.
which reaction or species the rate constant / half-life above describes, as the paper names it (at most 10 words), e.g. 'ImpA hydrolysis', 'Gly dimerization'.
the rate law or model the values come from, briefly (e.g. 'pseudo-first-order fit', 'consecutive reactions A -> B -> C, fitted', 'initial rates').

rules: Give rate constants in the unit printed (`u`), e.g. 's-1' or 'M-1 s-1'; the app converts. A rate constant whose order isn't 1 or 2 (or isn't stated) goes in `other` with its unit.
A rate measured per time interval for one species (mM/h) is a concentration change, not a rate constant: leave it out (the chemistry step records it).
Values of a fitted model of several reactions: the main or first constant in the parameters, the rest in `other`, one entry each, with the reaction they describe.
